name: RiverRun Logistics
arc_summary: RiverRun Logistics signed a 12-month pilot with Helix in early 2020, eager to test the new Helix API.  Despite a smooth initial integration, the carrier struggled with legacy ERP compatibility during the 2021 peak season, leading to a critical outage that prompted a pilot termination.  The loss highlighted the need for better legacy support in early releases and influenced Helix's subsequent microservices architecture shift.
contract_notes: The pilot contract stipulated a 30-day notice period, no upfront payment, and an SLA of 99% uptime.  No dedicated support was allocated for legacy ERP integration, which became a critical pain point during the 2021 surge.
referenced_in: Cited in 2023 sales retrospectives as the cautionary tale of early pilots that lacked legacy integration support.

name: Horizon Freight Solutions
arc_summary: Horizon Freight Solutions entered a pilot with Helix in early 2021, impressed by the API's flexibility. By mid-2022, they signed a multi-year contract and requested a custom integration for their legacy ERP. During the 2023 pitch for a full-scale rollout, Helix's new AI Optimizer feature was deemed too complex for Horizon's existing workflows, leading to a pitch loss and the customer's departure. The case highlighted the risk of over-customization and influenced Helix's later focus on modular plug-ins.
contract_notes: The contract promised 99.9% uptime SLA, with a $5,000 monthly fee and a 12-month commitment. Custom integration work was slated for a $20,000 one-time fee, which was later renegotiated to a lower rate after the pitch loss.
referenced_in: Cited in 2024 sales retro as the cautionary tale of over-customising for design partners.

name: Cascade Freight Partners
arc_summary: Cascade Freight Partners joined Helix in 2022 as a design partner for the Helix Dashboard, providing critical UI feedback that shaped the platform's user experience. In 2024 they helped beta-test the Helix AI Optimizer, but by early 2025 internal budget cuts led them to discontinue their partnership, citing that the new AI features did not align with their operational priorities. Their departure highlighted the risks of over-customising for design partners and prompted Helix to streamline its partner engagement model.
contract_notes: The contract included a custom UI integration clause, a 30-day SLA for uptime, and a monthly fee of $5,000 for a 12-month term.
referenced_in: Cited in 2024 sales retro as the cautionary tale of over-customising for design partners.

name: Glacier Freight Solutions
arc_summary: Glacier Freight Solutions signed a pilot agreement with Helix in early 2023, adopting the Helix API for their regional shipments. After the 2024 product redesign triggered by a critical customer escalation, the pilot was deemed incompatible with Glacier's operational workflow, leading to the pilot's termination in 2024 and the decision not to renew in 2025. Their departure prompted Helix to tighten pilot evaluation criteria and streamline onboarding for mid-market carriers.
contract_notes: The contract stipulated 30-day net payment terms, a 99.9% uptime SLA, and a custom real-time shipment tracking integration promised during the pilot phase.
referenced_in: Cited in the 2025 sales retrospective as a cautionary example of pilot dropoff that led to revised onboarding procedures.

name: Nimbus Freight Solutions
arc_summary: Nimbus Freight Solutions signed a pilot with Helix in early 2024, launching the "Nimbus Integration" project to embed Helix's API into their legacy dispatch system. In September 2024, Nimbus filed for bankruptcy after a liquidity crunch, prompting Helix to acquire the company in early 2025 to preserve the integration and salvage their routing algorithm. The acquisition allowed Helix to incorporate Nimbus's proprietary routing logic into the Helix AI Optimizer, boosting cost savings for flagship clients.
contract_notes: The contract included a 12-month pilot with a 10% discount on API usage, a 99.9% uptime SLA, and a custom routing module integration.
referenced_in: Referenced in 2025 product retrospective as the catalyst for Helix AI Optimizer's routing algorithm.

name: Highland Cargo Solutions
arc_summary: Highland Cargo Solutions signed on in early 2025, quickly adopting Helix AI Optimizer to streamline routing. However, the 2026 Series B funding round introduced new pricing tiers that increased their monthly fees, leading to a cost-overrun analysis and eventual churn in mid-2026. Their departure prompted Helix to revisit its tiered pricing model and add a mid-tier plan.
contract_notes: The 12-month contract offered a 10% discount for early renewal and guaranteed 99.9% uptime, but Highland requested a custom API integration that was delayed, contributing to their churn.
referenced_in: Referenced in 2027 sales training as a cautionary tale of mid-tier pricing adjustments post-Series B.

name: PeakLine Logistics
arc_summary: PeakLine Logistics signed a pilot agreement with Helix in 2020 and entered a formal pitch in early 2022. During the 2022 Q2 pitch meeting at their headquarters, Helix's pricing model was outbid by a competitor, leading to the loss of the account. The experience prompted Helix to redesign its pricing tiers and tighten its pitch deck for mid-market carriers.
contract_notes: The pilot contract stipulated a 12-month term with a 10% discount for early renewal, a 99.9% uptime SLA, and a custom API integration promised for real-time shipment tracking.
referenced_in: Cited in the 2024 sales retrospective as the cautionary tale that led to Helix's pricing strategy overhaul.

name: Summit Freight Partners
arc_summary: Summit Freight Partners joined Helix as a design partner in 2021, helping shape the early API and dashboard. After the 2023 product redesign triggered by a critical customer escalation, the partnership expanded to include a custom AI integration for route optimization. However, the increased cost of the AI module and a strategic shift toward larger enterprise clients led Summit to exit the partnership in 2025, citing budget constraints. Their departure prompted Helix to streamline its design partner program and focus on scalable, plug-in solutions.
contract_notes: The contract included a 12-month SLA with 99.9% uptime, a custom AI module at a premium rate, and a clause for co-development of new features.
referenced_in: Cited in 2024 sales retro as the cautionary tale of over-customising for design partners.

name: LogiBridge Solutions
arc_summary: LogiBridge Solutions signed a multi-year contract with Helix in 2022, expanding their freight operations with the Helix Dashboard. In 2024 a dispute erupted over an alleged SLA breach-LogiBridge claimed uptime fell to 99.5% during a critical shipment surge, while Helix maintained 99.9% compliance-leading to a formal escalation and eventual contract termination in 2025. The fallout prompted Helix to revise its SLA language and tighten uptime monitoring across all mid-market clients.
contract_notes: The contract stipulated 30-day net payment terms and a 99.9% uptime SLA, with custom real-time tracking integration promised for the flagship fleet. The dispute centered on Helix's failure to meet the uptime threshold during a 2024 shipment surge, which LogiBridge cited as a breach of contract.
referenced_in: Cited in the 2025 internal review as a cautionary example of SLA disputes leading to contract termination.

name: Summit Freight Solutions
arc_summary: Summit Freight Solutions signed on in early 2023, quickly adopting Helix Dashboard and later the Helix AI Optimizer.  The 2024 Q2 performance review highlighted integration issues with the AI Optimizer, prompting a costly redesign that strained the client's budget.  Despite a 2024 renewal, the company churned in 2025 following Helix's 15 % layoff and leadership shift, citing inability to justify the new AI features.
contract_notes: The contract stipulated 30-day payment terms and a 99.9% uptime SLA, with Helix promising a custom API integration for the client's legacy ERP system.
referenced_in: Cited in 2025 internal review as a cautionary example of mid-market churn after AI rollout.

name: RapidHaul Logistics
arc_summary: RapidHaul Logistics signed a pilot agreement in March 2024 to test Helix's real-time shipment tracking API.  Despite early enthusiasm, the pilot revealed integration gaps that required costly custom development, and by September 2025 the pilot was terminated without a renewal.  The experience highlighted the need for clearer scope definition in pilot contracts and influenced Helix's subsequent "Pilot Success Playbook."
contract_notes: The pilot contract stipulated 30-day payment terms, a 99.9% uptime SLA, and a custom API integration for real-time shipment tracking.  No full-scale license was signed, and the agreement included a clause allowing Helix to terminate the pilot if integration milestones were not met.
referenced_in: Cited in the 2025 sales retrospective as a cautionary tale of pilot misalignment leading to a missed renewal.

name: Crestline Freight Solutions
arc_summary: Crestline Freight Solutions signed a multi-year contract in early 2025, expanding its use of Helix's API to integrate with its legacy ERP. In mid-2026, a data breach incident triggered a formal escalation and a lawsuit alleging breach of the agreed 99.9% uptime SLA. The legal dispute forced Helix to renegotiate its contract terms and prompted a review of third-party integration security protocols. The case remains a reference point for Helix's compliance training.
contract_notes: The contract stipulated a 99.9% uptime SLA and a $200k annual fee with a 12-month payment schedule. Custom integration modules were promised to support legacy ERP connectors, but the agreement lacked explicit security audit clauses.
referenced_in: Mentioned in 2027 compliance audit report as a cautionary example of insufficient security clauses in custom integrations.

name: Riverstone Logistics
arc_summary: Riverstone Logistics began as a pilot partner in 2020, signing a full contract in 2021 after the successful Helix API rollout. In 2022 they renewed for another year, but during the 2023 Q2 sales pitch for the new Helix AI Optimizer, they chose a competitor offering lower pricing and deeper integration, leading to a lost pitch. The loss prompted Helix to tighten its competitive pricing strategy and refine its AI feature set for mid-market clients.
contract_notes: The contract called for a 12-month term with a 5% early renewal discount, a 99.9% uptime SLA, and custom API integration for real-time shipment tracking.
referenced_in: Cited in the 2024 sales retrospective as a cautionary tale of losing a mid-market client to a competitor during the Helix AI Optimizer launch.

name: Valley Freight Solutions
arc_summary: Valley Freight Solutions signed on in 2021, quickly adopting the Helix API during its early microservices rollout.  The 2021 near-miss outage exposed gaps in their integration, prompting a costly redesign that strained their budget.  By 2023, a critical escalation over SLA breaches led to a churn decision, marking a costly lesson in early-stage risk management for Helix.
contract_notes: The contract stipulated 30-day net payment terms and a 99.9% uptime SLA, with a custom API integration module promised to bridge legacy systems.
referenced_in: Cited in the 2024 sales retrospective as a cautionary tale of early API instability impacting mid-market clients.

name: Sierra Freight Solutions
arc_summary:
Sierra Freight Solutions joined Helix in 2022 as a design partner to co-develop the Helix Dashboard.  
After the 2023 product redesign and the 2024 launch of Helix AI Optimizer, the partner felt the platform no longer matched their operational model and opted to exit in 2025, citing misalignment of the feature roadmap.  
Their departure prompted a review of early-stage partner engagement and led to the creation of a dedicated partner success team.
contract_notes: The contract included a 12-month term with a 2-week SLA for custom AI Optimizer integration, net 30 payment terms, and a clause for joint roadmap reviews every quarter.
referenced_in: Cited in the 2026 Series B pitch deck as an example of early design partner feedback shaping the AI roadmap.

name: Canyon Freight Services
arc_summary: Canyon Freight Services joined Helix in early 2023 for a pilot focused on integrating the Helix API with their legacy dispatch system. The pilot, dubbed "Pilot Dropoff", ran through mid-2024 but was halted when Canyon cited resource constraints and a lack of promised SLA support. Despite a brief renewal offer in 2025, the company opted not to proceed, marking the end of their engagement. The experience prompted Helix to tighten pilot agreements and standardize SLA guarantees.
contract_notes: Pilot agreement included a 30-day payment term and a 99.9% uptime SLA, but no formal contract was signed; the pilot was intended to test API integration before a full subscription.
referenced_in: Cited in the 2025 internal post-mortem as a cautionary example of over-promising SLA during pilot phases.

name: Ridgeway Logistics
arc_summary: Ridgeway Logistics signed a pilot with Helix in early 2024, quickly expanding to a full contract after a successful API integration demo. In mid-2025, the company was acquired by Global Freight Holdings, leading Helix to terminate the account and re-allocate the custom feature work to other clients. The acquisition highlighted the risk of rapid scaling for mid-market partners and prompted Helix to tighten its partnership vetting process.
contract_notes: The contract promised a 30-day SLA for API uptime, net-15 payment terms, and a custom dashboard feature that was later repurposed for other mid-market clients after the acquisition.
referenced_in: Cited in the 2026 strategic partnership memo as a cautionary tale of rapid exit due to acquisition.

name: Evergreen Logistics
arc_summary: Evergreen Logistics signed a mid-tier Helix contract in early 2025, eager to leverage the new Helix AI Optimizer for route planning. In March 2026, a dispute erupted over Helix's 99.9% uptime SLA, as the company reported a series of unplanned outages that impacted critical shipments. The ensuing legal wrangling forced Helix to renegotiate its SLA language and add a data-governance clause, but Evergreen ultimately terminated the agreement in late 2026. The case prompted Helix to audit all mid-tier contracts for similar risk factors.
contract_notes: Evergreen paid 30-day net terms and was promised 99.9% uptime with a 24-hour response SLA for critical incidents. The contract also included a custom real-time shipment tracking integration that required Helix to expose API endpoints for third-party analytics.
referenced_in: Cited in the 2026 internal review as a cautionary tale for SLA enforcement and data governance in mid-tier contracts.
